manuscript_claim_text: Confirmatory adaptation hypothesis H-A achieves +1.0054 pp Macro-F1 (95% CI [-0.17, +1.99] pp, p=0.00131, 73.9% win rate), which is strictly INCONCLUSIVE under locked pre-registered decision rules.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Do not claim supported; do not claim superiority. Frame strictly as inconclusive within pre-registered [-0.17, +1.99] pp bounds.

manuscript_claim_text: FT-2 sleep-summary agreement shows non-significant bias for TST (+2.28 min), SOL (+3.20 min), SE (+0.47%), Deep% (+1.75%), and REM% (-2.16%), but significant empirical underestimation of WASO (-4.87 min, p < 0.05). Limits of agreement describe multi-night participant means.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Subject-averaged N=46 analysis evaluating multi-night means (~3 nights). Disclose empirical WASO underestimation without claiming intrinsic sensor limitation. Table 1 reports SE(LoA) and 95% CIs on LoA bounds.

manuscript_claim_text: Training personal models from scratch (PS-2) causes severe clinical distortion with large significant biases on SOL (-10.09 min, p < 0.001) and WASO (+12.08 min, p < 0.01).
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Within-cohort comparison demonstrating that population pre-training is required to stabilize hypnogram boundaries.

manuscript_claim_text: Personalized model tracks TST (r=0.9492) and SE (r=0.8775) strongly, but exhibits weak-to-moderate tracking for Deep% (r=0.4868) and REM% (r=0.4478).
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Bounds clinical claims: consumer IHR reliably tracks longitudinal multi-night sleep duration averages but is inadequate for resolving fine slow-wave architecture or isolated single-night spot values.

manuscript_claim_text: Hypothesis S1 is supported: personal fine-tuning outperforms donor fine-tuning by +2.73 pp Macro-F1 (p=0.00249, Wilcoxon p=1.89e-5), remaining robust (+2.87 pp, p=1.40e-5) when extreme outliers are excluded.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Establishes person-specific autonomic adaptation beyond generic fine-tuning artifacts.

manuscript_claim_text: Hypothesis S2 is supported: personal fine-tuning outperforms from-scratch personal models by +20.32 pp Macro-F1 (p=3.27e-19, Wilcoxon p=3.52e-9).
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Confirms that sample size of 2 nights is insufficient for de novo representation learning.

manuscript_claim_text: Hypothesis S3 is degenerate: UA-2 is bitwise identical to ZS across all 46 subjects (delta_S3 = 0.0 pp), representing an execution no-op that must be transparently disclosed.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Mandatory data-integrity disclosure. Unsupervised adaptation effect remains uncharacterized.

manuscript_claim_text: Detecting a true +1.0 pp personalization effect at 80% power requires approximately 107 multi-night subjects given paired delta SD of ~3.7 pp; N=46 cohorts are structurally underpowered.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Methodological power critique contextualizing small single-center digital health cohorts.

manuscript_claim_text: Study limitations include single-dataset scope (BIDSleep, 47 healthy adults), surrogate headband labels, aggregate-only microdata loss, empirical WASO underestimation, weak slow-wave r, S3 degeneracy, and absence of clinical/external validation.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Comprehensive risk and boundary disclosure (FIND-B-01, FIND-B-02, FIND-B-04). Disclaims clinical readiness, causal sensor claims, single-night spot precision, and external transfer.

manuscript_claim_text: Conclusion summarizes +1.01 pp inconclusive confirmatory gain, +2.73 pp specificity advantage, multi-night macro duration tracking vs slow-wave architecture limitations and empirical WASO underestimation.
claim_boundary_and_permissible_phrasing: Objective final synthesis adhering to locked empirical results without overclaiming; bounds clinical translation.
